BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook. I have treated the Seller's documents as counterparty material.

---

## 1. Threshold point: the Seller's framing

The covering preamble says the positions are "market standard", "settled at principal level by both deal teams", "agreed" and "FINAL… not intended to be re-opened." **We should not accept any of this.**

- Under playbook §0.4/§6.3, a counterparty document saying something is agreed, final or market does not make it so. Positions are only binding on us through our own authority process.
- I have seen no written authority from Amelia Frost approving any fallback for this draft. On our record, nothing has been "settled at principal level."
- The "market" ranges cited (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 month periods, buyer-knowledge qualifiers) are assertions with no support. They should not anchor the negotiation.
- **Recommended response:** state plainly in the cover note to our mark-up that Wattlebridge does not accept that any position is agreed or final, and that all points remain open pending our mark-up.

**Stale facts:** the Disclosure Letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**. Today is 5 November 2026. On Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar we should ask for a bring-down update and treat the September position as the last verified state. Any later "it's been dealt with" statement should be evidenced, not assumed.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue departures from the playbook

### A. Liability architecture

**1. General Warranty cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m**
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a conditional fallback needing Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft.
- **Issue:** the Seller has gone straight to our fallback number. That match does not clear it. No authority has been given, and the figure is presented as "agreed," which it is not.
- **Push back:** restore 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is available. If the team thinks movement may be needed later, escalate to Amelia Frost separately and in writing, naming this draft.

**2. Thresholds (cl 12.2): de minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k, excess only**
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; once exceeded, recovery from the first dollar.
- **Issue:** the de minimis is 5× ours and the basket is 5× ours. The "excess only" (deductible) structure would also permanently absorb the first AUD 250k of every claim stack. Combined with a 20% cap, this cuts our recoverable exposure sharply.
- **Push back:** AUD 5k / AUD 50k on a tipping basket. Fundamental, Title, fraud and specific-indemnity claims must sit outside both thresholds (see items 4 and 5).

**3. Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13): 18 months, plus "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"**
- **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Issue:** two separate problems.
  - (a) 18 months is an unapproved fallback.
  - (b) The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" sentence is a **hidden general-regime override**. It would pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenant and payment claims into the general limitations by default. That breaches the playbook rule that these categories stay separate.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims. Delete the default-to-all-Claims sentence. Each limitation should expressly state which claim category it covers.

**4. Fundamental / Title warranties: same caps and time limits as general warranties**
- **Playbook:** separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Issue:** this is a core departure. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for. Capping title at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month window is unacceptable.
- **Push back:** reject outright. Fundamental Warranties should be capped at 100% of price, run for at least six years, and sit outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge qualifier.

**5. Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5): "apply to all Claims of any nature"**
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-waivable.
- **Issue:** "all Claims of any nature" has no fraud carve-out. On its face it would try to shield the Seller from fraud and concealment claims, including through the non-reliance clause. It also catches specific indemnities, Tax and covenant claims.
- **Push back:** insert an express, overriding carve-out: *nothing in clauses 9.3, 12, 20.5 or elsewhere limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller or its Representatives.* Limit cl 12.8 and 20.5 to general Warranty Claims and carve out specific indemnities, Tax, Title and covenant claims. **This point should not be traded.**

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**6. Disclosure (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2): whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public records**
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Issue:** DL 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to" in the data room, including DD-002 to DD-012. DL 1.2 adds the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Together these would let the Seller argue that any document anywhere qualifies every warranty.
- **Push back:** delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 and the matching Schedule 7 language. Only matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, against a specific warranty, with enough detail for the Buyer to assess their nature and scope, should qualify the warranties. Fundamental Warranties should not be capable of qualification by disclosure.
- **DL 1.4 (non-admission):** a common protective clause. It should be confirmed that it cannot reduce the Seller's obligations under the SPA, for example by implying a consent or payment is "not required" where the SPA requires it.

**7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3): no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or that was discoverable from the data room or public records**
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Issue:** this is a blanket exclusion with constructive "discoverable" knowledge, extended to advisers. It would largely undo the warranties and indemnities, especially the specific indemnities we are seeking for matters we already know about (Ironquay, DD-006).
- **Push back:** delete cl 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should apply only to Seller knowledge, defined by named individuals after reasonable enquiry. It must never apply to Title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### C. Completion mechanics and identified risks

**8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3): "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery of written consent**
- **Playbook:** effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Consent-on-delivery is not enough, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Issue:** Bluefen is about **AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue** (DD-002). The Seller Update says the consent is "addressed," but **the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (item 2) says no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied has been provided.** The two documents contradict each other. Consent-on-delivery would let a conditional or ineffective consent satisfy the CP.
- **Push back:** make it a Condition Precedent, waivable only by the Buyer. Delivery of an unconditional, effective Bluefen consent under DD-002 cl 11.2 is required, together with documentary evidence that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied or irrevocably waived by Bluefen, before Completion. The Seller should carry a stronger obligation than reasonable endeavours (at least all reasonable endeavours) and keep the Buyer informed. Ask for the current status and correspondence now.

**9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): ~AUD 3.2m; release "following Completion"**
- **Playbook:** current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- **Issue:** a vague post-Completion release, with no undertaking and no approval, would leave security over the Company we are buying, on a debt-free/cash-free deal. DL item 3 confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge exists. DD-003 cl 8.1 (change of control) may also be triggered.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a payout letter dated close to Completion, with a daily rate.
  - Repayment should go directly to Riverlark from Completion funds, deducted from price.
  - Executed releases and discharges (including PPSR and any mortgages) should be delivered at Completion under DD-003 cl 9.2.
  - Any post-Completion element is a matter for Amelia Frost and would also require an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark. The Seller's draft provides neither.

**10. DD-005 Completion bonuses (funds flow): AUD 420k "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised**
- **Playbook:** AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or Seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Issue:** the bonuses are a Company liability triggered by Completion (DL item 5). Calling them "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow means the Company, and therefore the Buyer, would bear them. On-costs (payroll tax, super, PAYG withholding) are not addressed at all.
- **Push back:** add an express funds-flow line deducting AUD 420,000 plus all associated on-costs from price, paid via payroll. Alternatively, the Seller funds them, backed by a specific indemnity. Include them in the Debt / Transaction Costs definitions so they cannot drop out.

**11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1): indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate"**
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k is not independently verified either way.
- **Issue:** DD-004 cl 7.3 ties transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials to cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, but per DL item 4 that is not bank-verified. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. An indemnity covering only "the payment" leaves out infringement, loss of use, re-development cost and third-party claims if title to the IP has not passed.
- **Push back:** broaden the specific indemnity to cover all Losses from any failure of the Company to own, or hold valid rights to, the SOW3 (and wider Ironquay) materials. Keep the cure route: payment of any outstanding SOW3 fees, either pre-Completion or from a retention, plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable. Keep the indemnity outside caps, thresholds and the knowledge bar. Do not treat AUD 180k as a confirmed figure; ask for the payment ledger and bank evidence.

**12. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6): "preliminary… not expected to be material"**
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Issue:** the Seller's "not expected to be material" view is an unsupported assertion. The DL itself (item 6) says it is unknown whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope is unknown, and it is unknown whether notification is required. We should not accept immateriality. Equally, we should not treat it as a confirmed notifiable breach or put a dollar figure on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Add a pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs and evidence and complete a proper investigation, with any external forensic engagement subject to Buyer consultation.
  - Require regular written updates and Buyer consultation before any notification decision or regulator or third-party contact.
  - Add a specific indemnity for Losses arising from the incident, outside general limitations.
  - Remove the Seller's materiality characterisation from the SPA. Ask for a status update since 22 September.

**13. Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330k): "ordinary-course operating costs"**
- **Playbook:** assess. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Issue:** the Seller's ordinary-course label is not established. DL item 8 says it does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together on timing and scope, including possible related-party or splitting concerns. The opposite error should also be avoided: we should not assume these are Debt.
- **Push back:** request the contracts, approval records, term and termination rights, and accrual position. Hold the classification open: no ordinary-course concession and no Debt deduction until assessed. Add a warranty or conduct-of-business covenant on entry into and renewal of material contracts.

**14. Tax and IP warranties: "settled under the general regime"**
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Issue:** this is an attempt to declare open points closed and fold them into the general cap, basket and period.
- **Push back:** say expressly that Tax and IP terms remain open and are not agreed. Keep them as separate categories with their own regime to be negotiated. We are not asserting unlimited liability ourselves; we are simply keeping the point open.

**15. Title evidence: DD-012 share register**
- **Playbook:** independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not independent proof.
- **Issue:** DL item 10 itself concedes it only identifies the source relied on, not verification.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a current ASIC company extract, the original share certificates, and a PPSR search against the Seller and Company.
  - Require confirmation that there are no options, convertible instruments or third-party rights.
  - Require board and shareholder authorisations for the sale, executed share transfers, and evidence of discharge of any share security (linked to Riverlark).
  - Pair this with uncapped Title warranties under the Fundamental regime.

### D. Other Disclosure Letter items: verify, do not over-read

- **Office lease (DD-007):** the DL describes a notification obligation, not a consent requirement. Verify against the lease and make the notice a Completion deliverable or post-Completion covenant as appropriate. Do not assume a consent CP is needed.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** the DL describes an assignment restriction with no stated change-of-control trigger. Confirm from the contract that no change-of-control or deemed-assignment provision applies. Do not assume consent is needed, but do not rely solely on the Seller's reading.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Point | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Framing | "Agreed / FINAL / market" | Reject; all points open; no authority given |
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m**; 20% not available without Amelia Frost's written authority |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping** (first dollar) |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months; limits apply to all Claims by default | **24 months**; delete the default-to-all-Claims override |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | **100% cap, at least 6 years**, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge |
| 5 | Fraud | No carve-out; limits apply to "all Claims" | **Non-negotiable** carve-out from all limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance |
| 6 | Disclosure | Data room, registers, public records | **Specific fair disclosure only**; delete DL 1.1–1.2 |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, includes "discoverable" | **Delete**; any qualifier = named Seller persons plus reasonable enquiry; never Title, fraud or indemnities |
| 8 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | **CP: effective consent plus evidence cl 11.3 is satisfied**, pre-Completion; challenge "addressed" given DL item 2 |
| 9 | Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) | Release after Completion | **Payout letter, direct repayment from funds, releases at Completion**; any deferral needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost |
| 10 | DD-005 bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **Line item: AUD 420k plus on-costs**, or Seller-funded with indemnity |
| 11 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3-payment indemnity | **Broaden**; preserve SOW3 cure plus confirmatory assignment; AUD 180k unverified |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, updates, consultation, specific indemnity; no assumptions either way |
| 13 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | **Assess**; no ordinary-course concession, no automatic Debt deduction |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | **Remain OPEN**; separate regimes |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent evidence** (ASIC, PPSR, certificates, authorisations) |

**Priority order for the mark-up:**
1. Fraud carve-out.
2. Fundamental/Title regime and independent title evidence.
3. Removal of the hidden "all Claims" overrides (cl 12.3, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
4. Disclosure and buyer knowledge.
5. Completion-critical items: Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses.
6. Economics: cap, thresholds, period.
7. Specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006).
8. Open and assessment items: Tax/IP, Sandbar.

**Process actions:**
- (a) Send a bring-down information request covering Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay payment evidence, the DD-006 investigation status, and the Sandbar contracts, since the DL is dated 22 September.
- (b) Do not concede the 20% cap or 18-month period. If the team wants either as an option, raise it with Amelia Frost for written authority specific to this draft before it is mentioned to the Seller.
- (c) Flag the Bluefen inconsistency ("addressed" in the Update versus "NOT included" in the DL) to the Seller in writing.

- **Playbook:** separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Issue:** this is a core departure. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for. Capping title at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month window is unacceptable.
- **Push back:** reject outright. Fundamental Warranties should be capped at 100% of price, run for at least six years, and sit outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge qualifier.

**5. Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5): "apply to all Claims of any nature"**
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-waivable.
- **Issue:** "all Claims of any nature" has no fraud carve-out. On its face it would try to shield the Seller from fraud and concealment claims, including through the non-reliance clause. It also catches specific indemnities, Tax and covenant claims.
- **Push back:** insert an express, overriding carve-out: *nothing in clauses 9.3, 12, 20.5 or elsewhere limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller or its Representatives.* Limit cl 12.8 and 20.5 to general Warranty Claims and carve out specific indemnities, Tax, Title and covenant claims. **This point should not be traded.**

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**6. Disclosure (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2): whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public records**
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Issue:** DL 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to" in the data room, including DD-002 to DD-012. DL 1.2 adds the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Together these would let the Seller argue that any document anywhere qualifies every warranty.
- **Push back:** delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 and the matching Schedule 7 language. Only matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, against a specific warranty, with enough detail for the Buyer to assess their nature and scope, should qualify the warranties. Fundamental Warranties should not be capable of qualification by disclosure.
- **DL 1.4 (non-admission):** a common protective clause. It should be confirmed that it cannot reduce the Seller's obligations under the SPA, for example by implying a consent or payment is "not required" where the SPA requires it.

**7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3): no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or that was discoverable from the data room or public records**
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Issue:** this is a blanket exclusion with constructive "discoverable" knowledge, extended to advisers. It would largely undo the warranties and indemnities, especially the specific indemnities we are seeking for matters we already know about (Ironquay, DD-006).
- **Push back:** delete cl 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should apply only to Seller knowledge, defined by named individuals after reasonable enquiry. It must never apply to Title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### C. Completion mechanics and identified risks

**8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3): "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery of written consent**
- **Playbook:** effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Consent-on-delivery is not enough, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Issue:** Bluefen is about **AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue** (DD-002). The Seller Update says the consent is "addressed," but **the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (item 2) says no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied has been provided.** The two documents contradict each other. Consent-on-delivery would let a conditional or ineffective consent satisfy the CP.
- **Push back:** make it a Condition Precedent, waivable only by the Buyer. Delivery of an unconditional, effective Bluefen consent under DD-002 cl 11.2 is required, together with documentary evidence that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied or irrevocably waived by Bluefen, before Completion. The Seller should carry a stronger obligation than reasonable endeavours (at least all reasonable endeavours) and keep the Buyer informed. Ask for the current status and correspondence now.

**9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): ~AUD 3.2m; release "following Completion"**
- **Playbook:** current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- **Issue:** a vague post-Completion release, with no undertaking and no approval, would leave security over the Company we are buying, on a debt-free/cash-free deal. DL item 3 confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge exists. DD-003 cl 8.1 (change of control) may also be triggered.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a payout letter dated close to Completion, with a daily rate.
  - Repayment should go directly to Riverlark from Completion funds, deducted from price.
  - Executed releases and discharges (including PPSR and any mortgages) should be delivered at Completion under DD-003 cl 9.2.
  - Any post-Completion element is a matter for Amelia Frost and would also require an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark. The Seller's draft provides neither.

**10. DD-005 Completion bonuses (funds flow): AUD 420k "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised**
- **Playbook:** AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or Seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Issue:** the bonuses are a Company liability triggered by Completion (DL item 5). Calling them "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow means the Company, and therefore the Buyer, would bear them. On-costs (payroll tax, super, PAYG withholding) are not addressed at all.
- **Push back:** add an express funds-flow line deducting AUD 420,000 plus all associated on-costs from price, paid via payroll. Alternatively, the Seller funds them, backed by a specific indemnity. Include them in the Debt / Transaction Costs definitions so they cannot drop out.

**11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1): indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate"**
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k is not independently verified either way.
- **Issue:** DD-004 cl 7.3 ties transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials to cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, but per DL item 4 that is not bank-verified. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. An indemnity covering only "the payment" leaves out infringement, loss of use, re-development cost and third-party claims if title to the IP has not passed.
- **Push back:** broaden the specific indemnity to cover all Losses from any failure of the Company to own, or hold valid rights to, the SOW3 (and wider Ironquay) materials. Keep the cure route: payment of any outstanding SOW3 fees, either pre-Completion or from a retention, plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable. Keep the indemnity outside caps, thresholds and the knowledge bar. Do not treat AUD 180k as a confirmed figure; ask for the payment ledger and bank evidence.

**12. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6): "preliminary… not expected to be material"**
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Issue:** the Seller's "not expected to be material" view is an unsupported assertion. The DL itself (item 6) says it is unknown whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope is unknown, and it is unknown whether notification is required. We should not accept immateriality. Equally, we should not treat it as a confirmed notifiable breach or put a dollar figure on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Add a pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs and evidence and complete a proper investigation, with any external forensic engagement subject to Buyer consultation.
  - Require regular written updates and Buyer consultation before any notification decision or regulator or third-party contact.
  - Add a specific indemnity for Losses arising from the incident, outside general limitations.
  - Remove the Seller's materiality characterisation from the SPA. Ask for a status update since 22 September.

**13. Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330k): "ordinary-course operating costs"**
- **Playbook:** assess. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Issue:** the Seller's ordinary-course label is not established. DL item 8 says it does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together on timing and scope, including possible related-party or splitting concerns. The opposite error should also be avoided: we should not assume these are Debt.
- **Push back:** request the contracts, approval records, term and termination rights, and accrual position. Hold the classification open: no ordinary-course concession and no Debt deduction until assessed. Add a warranty or conduct-of-business covenant on entry into and renewal of material contracts.

**14. Tax and IP warranties: "settled under the general regime"**
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Issue:** this is an attempt to declare open points closed and fold them into the general cap, basket and period.
- **Push back:** say expressly that Tax and IP terms remain open and are not agreed. Keep them as separate categories with their own regime to be negotiated. We are not asserting unlimited liability ourselves; we are simply keeping the point open.

**15. Title evidence: DD-012 share register**
- **Playbook:** independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not independent proof.
- **Issue:** DL item 10 itself concedes it only identifies the source relied on, not verification.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a current ASIC company extract, the original share certificates, and a PPSR search against the Seller and Company.
  - Require confirmation that there are no options, convertible instruments or third-party rights.
  - Require board and shareholder authorisations for the sale, executed share transfers, and evidence of discharge of any share security (linked to Riverlark).
  - Pair this with uncapped Title warranties under the Fundamental regime.

### D. Other Disclosure Letter items: verify, do not over-read

- **Office lease (DD-007):** the DL describes a notification obligation, not a consent requirement. Verify against the lease and make the notice a Completion deliverable or post-Completion covenant as appropriate. Do not assume a consent CP is needed.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** the DL describes an assignment restriction with no stated change-of-control trigger. Confirm from the contract that no change-of-control or deemed-assignment provision applies. Do not assume consent is needed, but do not rely solely on the Seller's reading.
